summary.text: The Department of State’s enterprise AI strategy states that it will use data and AI to strengthen diplomacy, improve mission effectiveness, and drive operational efficiency. In February 2026, the Department announced a pilot “concierge” service to help Pax Silica signatories acquire American-made AI products and said it would provide logistical and consultative support to trusted partner nations and industry leaders. The Department has described AI governance measures, including strengthened governance bodies and implementation at executive, strategic, tactical, and operational levels, and it developed a Risk Management Profile for AI and Human Rights with NIST and USAID. Its supplied statements also describe international AI frameworks and cooperation, including endorsed rules for responsible military AI use, a UN General Assembly resolution on safe, secure, and trustworthy AI, and a G7 multilateral framework for advanced AI developers.

autonomous_weapons.why: Endorsement of responsible military AI principles does not specify human control of lethal force or limits on lethal autonomous weapons.

superintelligence.why: Support for advancing superintelligence and mitigating its harms does not establish support for or opposition to a ban on building it.
